talks.title: Your AI Product Will Fail Unless You Can Explain It

quotes.quote: And in this market, that shot lasts about the time it takes to ride an elevator.
What is the exact moment your user wants to throw their laptop out a window?
To demonstrate their wound, follow one rule. Do not start with what you built.
The very first slide of your pitch should immerse people in their day-to-day of their job. And show them what they are already tired of doing.
The format is simple. In about 20 seconds, you need to do three things. Identify the wound, say we fix that, then show how.
Once you've shown them the wound, your next job is to make the product click. Here's the test. Could a 17-year-old understand what you do? If not, you're probably going to lose the room.
One of the fastest ways to fix that is to tie your product to a viral story people already understand.
If McDonald's had used us, that drive-thru never would have made it to TikTok. We catch when AI agents go off script and give teams a chance to correct them before it becomes a PR nightmare.
You can give the technical version later to close the sale. Just don't make it the first thing people have to understand.

A lot of founders will say things like, "We improve code quality with AI." or "We increase productivity." That sounds nice, but I still do not know what actually changes for me once your product enters my world.
Before your support team spends 30 minutes digging through docs and tickets, with us, they ask one question and get the answer in 10 seconds with the sources attached.
15 years ago, if you built something great, the market might have found you.
Identify the wound, make your product click, show the transformation, then your idea won't fail

positions.claim: Many AI products are failing in the market primarily because their pitches are incomprehensible, not because the technology is inadequate.
A pitch should open with the customer's pain rather than with a description of what the company built.
The wound, the fix, and the how can and should be delivered in roughly 20 seconds.
If a 17-year-old cannot understand what your product does, you will lose the room.
Imprecise but vivid descriptions are acceptable — even preferable — as an opening, because technical precision can be supplied later in the sales conversation.
Buzzword-laden category language like 'agentic AI orchestration platform' or 'agent observability platform' actively harms comprehension and should not be used to open.
Abstract benefit statements such as 'we increase productivity' fail to convey value; only a concrete before/after comparison does.
Product quality alone no longer generates market discovery the way it did roughly 15 years ago; clarity of story now determines which products get funded and bought.
Anchoring a pitch to an already-viral public incident is one of the most efficient ways to make an unfamiliar product category legible.
